item.stem:
The diagram shows square $S$ of side $3\,\mathrm{cm}$ and square $T$ of side $6\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Which claim correctly states how the area changes from $S$ to $T$?

options.A: The area of $T$ is twice the area of $S$ because the side length doubled.
options.B: The area of $T$ is four times the area of $S$ because the side length doubled.
options.C: The area of $T$ equals the area of $S$ because both shapes are squares.
options.D: The area of $T$ is six times the area of $S$, matching the new side length.
